scope: ADR-019 clauses 1-5 and 7: global BadgePosition (TopLeft/TopRight/BottomLeft/BottomRight/Center; default BottomLeft) and BadgeSize (Small/Medium/Large; default Medium); effectiveScale = clamp(width/1000, 0.5, 4.0) * sizeFactor (0.75/1.0/1.5) with safe-area clamp; per-anchor rail packing and status-pill placement; position/size on RenderOutputPolicy and in both fingerprints; settings-page exposure.

findings.description: The top-anchor status-pill reservation is not exercised, and the test named for it cannot fail if the reservation is removed. BadgeLayoutEngine reserves the status pill plus one gap from the first rail row only for top anchors (rowAvailableWidth[0] = safeWidth - statusPill.Width - pillGap, BadgeLayoutEngine.cs:80-87). BadgeSizePositionTests.TopAnchorsReserveTheTopRowForTheStatusPill uses CustomValues(6) with a 2-char pill (~44 px) and a ~94 px status pill on a 1000 px poster, so the top-left rail can never reach the opposite-side status pill and the reservation boundary is never reached. Removing the reservation entirely leaves the full default suite green (Failed 0, Passed 1490, Skipped 63, Total 1553). A throwaway wide-pill probe (3 x ~300 px pills, TopLeft, ~208 px status pill on 1000x1500) passes pristine and fails with the reservation removed: 'status 768..976 overlaps pill at 640..940'. The reservation is therefore a real, undocumented-in-tests behaviour.
evidence: Mutation M7 (rowAvailableWidth[0] = safeWidth) -> full suite Failed 0, Passed 1490, Skipped 63, Total 1553 (no committed test failed)
Throwaway /tmp probe WideTopLeftRailDoesNotOverlapTheTopRightStatusPill: pristine Failed 0/Passed 1; reservation removed Failed 1/Passed 0 with 'status 768..976 overlaps pill at 640..940'
findings.recommended_action: Add a top-anchor case with pills wide enough that the first rail row would collide with the status pill absent the reservation (combined first-row width > safeWidth - statusPill.Width - pillGap but <= safeWidth) and assert non-overlap. Also narrow the theory to top anchors or rename it, since the bottom/center InlineData cases have an empty top band and are vacuous.

findings.description: The ADR-019 clause 6 identity-neutral default fingerprint claim has no unguarded absolute pin. The committed tests only compare the code-owned default against an explicit (BottomLeft, Medium) policy through the same code path, so they pass when the default fingerprint itself changes. Making AppendBadgePlacement append unconditionally in both RenderFingerprint.ComputeOutputFingerprint and RendererConfigurationFingerprint.Compute (so the default output and configuration fingerprints change) leaves the full default suite green (Failed 0, Passed 1490, Skipped 63, Total 1553). The only absolute check is RenderGoldenTests.GoldenMatchesDecodedPixelsBytesDimensionsAndFingerprint, which compares the committed Goldens/manifest.json OutputFingerprint, and that test is native-Skia-skipped in the shipping configuration. The manifest OutputFingerprint comparison itself requires no native Skia, so an unguarded pin is feasible today.

mutation_or_non_vacuity_evidence.default_geometry_assessment: The pure layout tests genuinely pin the default bottom-left geometry numerically, not relatively: DefaultPolicyReproducesTheV1BottomLeftGeometry asserts Scale 1.0, X 24, Y height-24-48, Height 48, Row 0; EachAnchorPlacesTheRailAtTheExpectedCornerOrCenter(BottomLeft), BottomAnchorsStackRowsUpwardFromTheBottomEdge, LeftAnchorsAlignRowsToTheLeftEdge, and the pre-existing RendererBehaviorLayoutTests.TheTechnicalRailSitsAtTheBottomLeft / TechnicalRailSitsAtTheBottomInsideTheSafeArea assert absolute coordinates. The code-owned RenderOutputPolicy.Default (BottomLeft, Medium) is additionally pinned by RendererConfigurationTests.ResolverFallsBackToDefaultsForUndefinedBadgePositionAndSize (asserts the fallback equals both Default and the literal BottomLeft/Medium). Mutations M1, M3, M5, M6, M8, M10 all fail, so a default-path geometry/scale regression is caught without native Skia.
mutation_or_non_vacuity_evidence.residual_risk: Only task 12.4's golden regeneration can close the end-to-end pixel/byte comparison and the absolute default-fingerprint pin: the committed golden pixel comparison and the manifest OutputFingerprint comparison both live in the native-Skia-guarded RenderGoldenTests, which is skipped in the shipping configuration. A subtle renderer-only change to the default output that leaves the pure layout geometry and the policy inputs unchanged (for example a draw-time padding/font change) is not caught by any unguarded test.

assertion_strength: The new tests assert observable layout geometry (pill X/Y/Width/Height/Row and layout.Scale), status-pill placement and non-overlap, absolute per-anchor coordinates, fingerprint equality/inequality, validator errors, and resolver output. They do not assert private/internal flags. The only source-string assertions are the config.html settings-page exposure, which matches the repository's established pattern for the static page.
determinism_checked: No wall-clock, random, network, filesystem-order, or process-state dependence in BadgeSizePositionTests, the new RenderFingerprintTests fact, the new RendererConfigurationTests facts, or the new DashboardSettingsPageTests fact; all are pure in-memory calls with fresh inputs.
No ambient culture dependence: invariant formatting is used (index.ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)); the layout delegates are deterministic (text.Length * 10f / * 92f).

InlineData enum and double arguments are compile-time constants; floating-point assertions use explicit precision (3 or 6 digits) and epsilon-bounded InRange checks, so no incidental exact-double fragility was observed.
Tests are isolated: no shared mutable state between cases; the new facts construct fresh PluginConfiguration/RenderOutputPolicy instances.
substitutes_checked: BadgeLayoutEngine is measured through a caller-supplied Func<string,float> delegate instead of a raster font, so the pure layout tests never load Skia; the renderer consumes the same layout placements and ComputeEffectiveScale (SkiaBadgeRenderer.cs:201, :214-220), so the substitute covers the layout math but not draw-time pixels.

RendererConfigurationIntegrationTests uses an in-memory FingerprintingRenderer instead of SkiaBadgeRenderer; it exercises the real snapshot/resolver/coordinator path and the fingerprint inputs, not decoded pixels.
The native Skia pixel/byte path is entirely native-guarded and skipped in this environment.

summary: Task 12.3's test suite is substantially non-vacuous and honest: 13 targeted mutations show that the size factors, the TopRight status-pill rule, per-anchor horizontal alignment and vertical stacking, the safe-area clamp, both fingerprint inclusions, undefined-value validation, the resolver fallback, and settings-page exposure all fail when broken, and the default bottom-left geometry/scale is pinned by absolute-coordinate assertions (mutations M1/M3/M5/M6/M8/M10 fail). The full default suite reproduces exactly Failed 0, Passed 1490, Skipped 63, Total 1553, the focused filter 142/2/144, and BadgeSizePositionTests 39/0/39; all 63 skips are environment-guarded (native Skia / pinned Jellyfin host) with zero new skips. Three gaps remain: (MEDIUM) the top-anchor status-pill reservation is real - a wide-pill probe shows removing it overlaps the status pill - yet no committed test fails when it is removed, so the test named for it is non-failing; (MEDIUM) the ADR-019 clause 6 identity-neutral default fingerprints are only tested relatively, so an unconditional fingerprint append passes the whole unguarded suite, with the only absolute pin in the native-skipped golden test; (LOW) the Center-anchor status-band row-reduction branch is never exercised (the equivalent bottom-anchor branch is guarded by a pre-existing test). None of these blocks 12.4; the two default-preservation items are naturally closed by 12.4's coordinated RenderVersion/schema advance and golden regeneration, and the reservation/Center cases are cheap test additions worth making.
